bullets.text: A waterborne disease outbreak affected the Ondaraya Delta from early June 2025, centred on Kelvaig village and the southern wards of Serriport.
The likely source was an interruption of chlorination at the Meskin Reservoir intake during pump repairs, with untreated canal water used in Kelvaig during the gap.
The response combined a 60-bed treatment centre, emergency chlorination and a delta-wide boil-water notice, and the outbreak was assessed as contained by June 6.
Residents of Kelvaig report widespread vomiting and cramps; Serriport District Hospital notes an unusual number of severe diarrhoea cases.
Ondaraya Health Directorate announces an investigation into a cluster of acute watery diarrhoea cases.
First official count: 34 suspected cases recorded; samples sent for laboratory testing.
Delta Water Board discloses a 48-hour interruption of chlorination at the Meskin Reservoir intake during pump repairs.
A suspected cholera outbreak is publicly reported; suspected cases rise to 76 with two deaths under investigation.
Laboratory results identify Vibrio cholerae in 11 of the first 15 samples; NERU deploys an epidemiological team and medical supplies.
Suspected case count peaks at 148 under a broad case definition; a 60-bed cholera treatment centre opens at the Serriport fairground.
Delta Water Board begins emergency chlorination and issues a delta-wide boil-water notice.
NERU reports that 89 of the 148 suspected cases are laboratory-confirmed, with the remainder reclassified to other causes.
OHD confirms 4 cholera deaths and states that two earlier reported deaths were from unrelated causes.
The first daily coordination meeting between OHD and Riverlands Health Trust agrees case-definition and reporting procedures.
Two deaths were initially reported as under investigation during the early phase of the outbreak.
Four deaths were subsequently confirmed as caused by cholera.
Two of the earlier reported deaths were determined to be from unrelated causes and were excluded from the outbreak toll.
The first official count recorded 34 suspected cases of acute watery diarrhoea across the delta.
Suspected cases rose to 76 and then to 148 under a broad case definition covering all acute watery diarrhoea.
Laboratory testing confirmed 89 cases of cholera among the 148 investigated, with the remainder reclassified to other causes.
Serriport District Hospital reached ward capacity and opened an overflow tent in its car park.
Forty-one patients were admitted at the peak of the reported admissions figures.
New admissions fell for two consecutive days before the outbreak was assessed as contained.
Chlorination at the Meskin Reservoir intake was interrupted for 48 hours during pump repairs in the week before the outbreak.
The Kelvaig clinic exhausted its stock of oral rehydration salts early in the outbreak.
Schools in Kelvaig and southern Serriport were closed for the week as a precaution.
A boil-water notice was issued for all Ondaraya Delta connections.
Emergency chlorination was started and chlorine residual returned to target range at the reservoir outlet.
Households in Tanmere were cut off by the flooded canal path and were reached by a volunteer boat service.
Laboratory testing identified Vibrio cholerae in 11 of the first 15 samples analysed.
The health directorate stated there was no evidence of deliberate contamination of the reservoir.
The Ondaraya Health Directorate opened an investigation into the case cluster and issued water safety advisories.
The National Epidemic Response Unit deployed an epidemiological team and two tonnes of medical supplies to Serriport.
A 60-bed cholera treatment centre was opened at the Serriport fairground, jointly run with Riverlands Health Trust.
The Delta Water Board began emergency chlorination and issued a delta-wide boil-water notice.
The health directorate advised residents not to drink untreated canal water and to boil water for at least one minute or use purification tablets.
A boil-water notice was issued for all delta connections and remained in force pending clear samples.
The health directorate issued daily briefings recording confirmed cases, deaths and current admissions.
Officials publicly rejected a rumour that the reservoir had been deliberately poisoned, attributing the outbreak to a treatment interruption.
Residents publicly appealed for assistance as hospital wards filled during the early phase.
Riverlands Health Trust deployed a mobile rehydration team to Kelvaig with oral rehydration salts and intravenous fluids.
Ondaraya Red Wave Society volunteers distributed water purification tablets door to door in Kelvaig and 4,200 household purification kits across the delta.
The National Epidemic Response Unit delivered two tonnes of medical supplies to Serriport alongside its epidemiological team.
The Kelvaig clinic exhausted its oral rehydration salt stock before resupply, leaving demand unmet during the early phase.
Households in Tanmere cut off by the flooded canal path received supplies via a volunteer boat service.
The health directorate and Riverlands Health Trust held the first daily coordination meeting at the Serriport district office, agreeing case-definition and reporting procedures.
Volunteers in Tanmere organised a boat service to deliver supplies to cut-off households.
Residents expressed alarm at the speed of the outbreak and frustration at shortages of rehydration salts.
Public gratitude was expressed toward treatment centre staff and health workers conducting household checks.
